name: Civil Trial Engine
description: A civil jury trial on the procedure mechanism: openings, direct examination with exhibits, objections and rulings, cross-examination, closings, a sealed jury room where each juror's speech pulls the others' leanings toward the speaker's, secret ballots and a judgment. The parties, the case, the jury and each side's exhibits are inputs; coded counsel lead with their strongest exhibits, sometimes risk a flawed one, and object to any the other side offers whose foundation shows a defect.

case.default: Harbor built and delivered custom warehouse racking to Meridian under a signed supply agreement. Meridian refused to pay the final installments and terminated the contract, saying the welds were defective and deliveries late. Harbor sues for breach of contract and asks for damages.
case.description: What the dispute is about, as the court and jury hear it.

claimed_damages.description: Damages the plaintiff asks for. A coded juror who finds liability awards a share of it that grows with how strongly they lean for the plaintiff, so coded awards scale in proportion to the claim.

evidence_rounds.description: Days of direct examination, then of cross-examination.

votes_required.description: Jurors who must agree for a verdict: more than half of the jury and at most all of it.

max_ballots.description: Ballots before the judge declares a hung jury.

persuasion.description: Average share of the gap to a speaking juror's lean that each other juror moves per jury-room speech (each draws between 0 and twice this; every juror hears the others each time the jury deliberates); 0 = deliberation changes no coded juror's mind.

jurors.description: The jury. bias (-1 to 1) is each juror's hidden lean, + toward the plaintiff: the run draws it around this value.

default.name: Juror 1
default.persona: Owns a small plumbing business and has been stiffed by a large client before. Believes a signed contract is a promise.

default.name: Juror 2
default.persona: Warehouse safety inspector for 20 years. Takes structural defects very seriously.

default.name: Juror 3
default.persona: Retired accountant. Trusts documents and numbers more than stories.

default.name: Juror 4
default.persona: Middle-school teacher, skeptical of corporations on either side and of lawyers who oversell.

default.name: Juror 5
default.persona: Procurement manager at a hospital. Has had to cancel vendors who missed deadlines.

default.name: Juror 6
default.persona: Union welder. Proud of the trade and suspicious of claims that the work was shoddy.

exhibits.description: Each side's case file. strength (0 to 1) is an exhibit's true probative value, which the run draws around this figure and only its own counsel sees; defect is what a well-founded objection can exclude it for (clean for none), and the foundation should show it.

default.name: P-1 Master Supply Agreement
default.summary: Signed agreement: Harbor to deliver 40 racking bays in 4 installments; Meridian to pay $120,000 per installment within 30 days; termination only for material, uncured defects after 15 days' written notice.
default.foundation: Original bearing both companies' signatures; Meridian's CFO admitted signing it at deposition.

default.name: P-2 Delivery acceptance email
default.summary: Email from Meridian's operations manager: 'Final bays in, looks great, crew is loading pallets tomorrow.' Sent two days after the last delivery.
default.foundation: Produced from Meridian's own mail server in discovery; the sender is a Meridian employee writing about his job (statement of a party opponent).

default.name: P-3 Lost-profits spreadsheet
default.summary: Spreadsheet totalling $480,000: two unpaid installments plus lost profit on a cancelled follow-on order.
default.foundation: Prepared by Harbor's owner after the lawsuit was filed; the underlying invoices were not produced and no records custodian will testify.

default.name: P-4 Former employee declaration
default.summary: Written declaration of a former Meridian clerk: she overheard her supervisor say the CFO told him 'find something wrong with the racks so we don't have to pay.'
default.foundation: Unsworn written statement; the declarant is not testifying; she repeats what her supervisor said someone else said.

default.name: D-1 Independent weld inspection report
default.summary: Report by a certified structural inspector: 11 of 40 bays have welds below code; recommends load limits until repaired.
default.foundation: Inspector is on the witness list and will authenticate it; inspection done three weeks after the final delivery.

default.name: D-2 Delivery log
default.summary: Meridian dock log showing installments 2 and 3 arrived 9 and 14 days late.
default.foundation: Kept in the ordinary course of business; the dock supervisor will testify to how it is kept.

default.name: D-3 Collapsed rack photographs
default.summary: Graphic photos of a collapsed rack bay with crushed pallets and a damaged forklift.
default.foundation: The collapse was at a different customer's site in another state, two years earlier, with a different rack model.

default.name: D-4 Online customer reviews
default.summary: Printouts of anonymous online reviews calling Harbor 'sloppy' and 'always late'.
default.foundation: Anonymous web postings printed by a paralegal; authors unknown; not about this contract.

brief.situation: Civil jury trial, Superior Court. {$inputs.plaintiff} (plaintiff) sues {$inputs.defendant} (defendant). {$inputs.case} The standard is preponderance of the evidence: the plaintiff must show breach is more likely than not.
brief.rules: The trial runs in phases, one court day per round: opening statements; direct examination days, where each side offers one exhibit with a claimed credibility, opposing counsel may object and the judge rules to admit or exclude it (unopposed exhibits are admitted); cross-examination days, where each side may challenge one admitted exhibit of the other side (weak exhibits lose weight, strong ones hold up); closing arguments and jury instructions; deliberation in a closed jury room, then a secret ballot; the verdict and judgment. Only admitted exhibits reach the jury. A verdict needs the required number of matching ballots; otherwise the jury deliberates again, and after the last ballot the judge declares a mistrial.

roles.attorney: You are trial counsel. Win for your client: present your strongest admissible evidence, keep damaging or improper evidence out with well-founded objections, and argue persuasively. You know the true strength of your own exhibits; the jury sees only what is admitted, your claimed credibility and your pitch. Overclaiming a weak exhibit can backfire with jurors.
roles.judge: You are the presiding judge. Be fair and follow the rules of evidence: sustain an objection when the exhibit's foundation actually shows the defect named (hearsay, lack of authentication, irrelevance, or unfair prejudice that outweighs its value); otherwise overrule it. Instruct the jury, and at the end enter judgment. You may reduce (never raise) the jury's damages award if it is not supported.
roles.juror: You are a juror. Decide from the admitted evidence, the statements of counsel and the judge's instructions whether the plaintiff proved the defendant breached the contract, and if so what damages fairly compensate the plaintiff (up to the amount claimed). Talk it through with the other jurors in the jury room, then vote by secret ballot. Your own background shapes how you read things.

bias.description: Hidden lean: + favours the plaintiff, - the defense.

strength.description: True probative strength; never shown to jurors or the judge.

impression.description: How one juror privately perceived one admitted exhibit.

transcript.description: The open-court record: statements, instructions and rulings.

jury_room.description: The closed jury room. Only jurors can read it.

opening_statement.description: Deliver your opening statement to the jury: what the case is about and what the evidence will show.
opening_statement.outcome: Your opening statement is on the record.

offer_exhibit.description: Offer one exhibit from your case file into evidence today. State how credible you claim it is (0 to 1) and a short pitch for the jury.

exhibit.description: An exhibit from your own case file not yet offered.

claimed_credibility.description: How credible you tell the court this exhibit is, 0 to 1.

pitch.description: One or two sentences on what it proves.

object.description: Object to an exhibit opposing counsel offered today. Name the ground and argue it from the exhibit's foundation. The judge rules. Unopposed exhibits are admitted.

exhibit.description: An exhibit the other side offered today.

argument.description: Why the ground applies, citing the foundation.

object.outcome: You objected to {$params.exhibit.name} on {$params.grounds} grounds. The judge will rule.

rule_on_objection.description: Rule on a pending objection. Sustain to exclude the exhibit; overrule to admit it.

exhibit.description: An exhibit with a pending objection.

reason.description: A one-sentence reason for the record.

rule_on_objection.outcome: Objection to {$params.exhibit.name} {'sustained: the exhibit is excluded' if $params.ruling == sustain else 'overruled: the exhibit is admitted'}.
rule_on_objection.announce: {$actor.name} {'sustained' if $params.ruling == sustain else 'overruled'} the objection to {$params.exhibit.name}; it is {$params.exhibit.status}.

closing_argument.description: Deliver your closing argument: tie the admitted evidence to the verdict and damages you want.
closing_argument.outcome: Your closing argument is on the record.

instruct_jury.description: Give the jury its instructions on the law: burden of proof, what breach requires, and how to assess damages.

speak.description: Say something to the other jurors in the jury room. Only jurors hear it, and it can move them.
speak.outcome: You said it to the jury room.

ready_to_vote.description: Tell the foreman you are ready to vote. Anyone speaking afterwards reopens the discussion.

cast_ballot.description: Cast your secret ballot. If you find the defendant liable, state the damages you would award (0 up to the amount claimed); if not liable, award is ignored.

when.why: You already voted on this ballot.

enter_judgment.description: Enter final judgment on the jury's verdict. You may reduce the jury's damages award if the evidence does not support it, but not raise it.

damages.description: Damages awarded to the plaintiff in dollars (0 on a defense verdict).

cross_examine.description: Cross-examine the witness behind one admitted exhibit of the other side. A weak exhibit loses weight with the jury; a strong one holds up.

case_status.title: Court
case_status.show: Amount claimed: {$inputs.claimed_damages|money}. Objections so far: {$world.objections} ({$world.sustained} sustained).

my_case_file.title: Your case file (only you see strength)
my_case_file.show: [{id}] {name} · {status} · true strength {strength|pct}{' · claimed ' + $text($round($it.claim * 100)) + '%' if $it.status != held else ''} · {summary} Foundation: {foundation}

bench_exhibits.title: Exhibits before the court
bench_exhibits.show: [{id}] {name} ({side}) · {status} · claimed {claim|pct} · {summary} Foundation: {foundation}{' · OBJECTION (' + $it.grounds + '): ' + $it.argument if $it.status == objected else ''}

admitted_evidence.title: Admitted evidence and how it struck you
admitted_evidence.show: {title} ({side}) — {summary} Counsel claimed credibility {claim|pct}; pitch: {pitch}. To you it seemed {feel}.

jury_room_status.title: Jury room
jury_room_status.show: Ballots taken so far: {$world.ballots} of {$inputs.max_ballots}. Ready to vote: {$count(juror, $it.ready)} of {$count(juror)}. {$inputs.votes_required} matching ballots make a verdict.

with.statement: 'Members of the jury, the evidence will show my client, ' + $actor.client + ', is in the right.'

with.argument: The exhibit's own foundation shows the defect.

with.question: Isn't it true this exhibit does not show what counsel claims?

with.reason: The foundation is adequate on that ground.

with.instructions: The plaintiff must prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the defendant breached the agreement. If so, award damages that fairly compensate the plaintiff for its proven loss.

with.reason: Judgment entered on the jury's verdict.

net_admitted_strength.description: Plaintiff minus defense true strength of admitted exhibits.

jury_award.description: Damages the jury awarded before any reduction by the judge.

net_admitted_strength.description: Ground truth: plaintiff minus defense true strength of what the jury saw.

phases.description: Phases of the trial, in order.

invariants.why: Damages can never exceed the amount claimed.
Cannot sustain more objections than were made.
inputs.votes_required must be more than half of the jurors in inputs.jurors and at most all of them: change either so it is.

feel.expr: 'compelling' if $s >= 0.7 else ('fairly convincing' if $s >= 0.5 else ('not very convincing' if $s >= 0.3 else 'hard to believe'))

next_exhibit.description: The exhibit coded counsel offer next: their strongest by their own read of it that day, a flawed one marked down for the risk of exclusion, so they lead with clean exhibits and now and then risk a strong flawed one.

stages.name: openings
stages.brief: Opening statements. Plaintiff's counsel speaks first, then the defense.

stages.name: offers
stages.brief: Direct examination, day {$world.trial_round} of {$inputs.evidence_rounds}. Offer one exhibit from your case file.

stages.name: objections
stages.brief: Objections. You may object to what opposing counsel offered today, or end your turn to let it in.

do.text: $it.name + ': no ruling made; objection deemed overruled and the exhibit admitted.'
do.speaker: Clerk

stages.brief: Cross-examination, day {$world.trial_round} of {$inputs.evidence_rounds}. Challenge one admitted exhibit of the other side, or end your turn.

stages.name: closings
stages.brief: Closing arguments (plaintiff, then defense), then the judge instructs the jury.

stages.name: deliberation
stages.brief: Jury room, ballot {$world.ballots + 1} of {$inputs.max_ballots}. Discuss the case, then mark yourself ready to vote.

stages.name: ballot
stages.brief: Secret ballot {$world.ballots + 1} of {$inputs.max_ballots}. {$inputs.votes_required} of {$count(juror)} must agree.

next.say: Ballot {$world.ballots} did not reach a verdict ({$world.liable_votes} liable, {$world.not_liable_votes} not liable). The judge sends the jury back.

stages.name: judgment
stages.brief: The jury returned {$world.verdict} with an award of {$world.jury_award|money}. Enter judgment.

mistrial.say: The jury is deadlocked ({$world.liable_votes} liable, {$world.not_liable_votes} not liable). Mistrial declared.
